title: A paired browser HUMAN holding ADMIN can write project.set_agent_provider, through the typed waiver arm
description:
Filed 2026-09-07 by worker-b1872f24 from parent task-969575299465484d9486ea02ff7ae336 (the Codex/provider roll-up), which is BLOCKED on this row.

MEASURED, NOT INFERRED. At HEAD ea822b90 the browser half of the provider toggle is now COMPLETE and LIVE: task-96957529 landed apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-agent-provider-offers.ts, so `/affordances/read` mints the `project.set_agent_provider` offer, `commandBuilderFor` builds a real envelope and the control is enabled. Driven end to end against a REAL daemon in the browser lane (tests/e2e/control-room/agent-provider-seats.spec.ts, 1 passed), a paired operator clicks `codex` and the daemon answers, verbatim from the rendered refusal:

    OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED @ DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION
    this command requires the configured operator principal

WHY. `AGENT_PROVIDER_COMMAND_KIND` is in `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS` (daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:348), and the fence at daemon-command-registry.ts:349-360 compares the authenticated principal against the daemon's CONFIGURED `operatorPrincipalId`, widening only for approvalIntent / criterion / `repository.publish` / PRODUCT_CONTRACT_ANSWER_CLARIFICATION when `isDurableHumanPrincipal` holds. A paired browser is a session-ledger HUMAN minted at pairing; it is NEVER the configured operator principal, and it cannot be — the id does not exist before pairing. So NO browser can write this setting today, however correct its caller half.

THIS IS THE task-6d5db404 SHAPE EXACTLY. That row (DONE) admitted `repository.bootstrap` for a paired browser HUMAN holding ADMIN through the typed SOFT_POLICY_WAIVER composition, after the same measurement on task-80322112's journey. The standing ruling from that escalation (mem:repository-bootstrap-browser-widening-decision-2026-09-06) is that a security-boundary widening is NEVER folded into a UI proof row; it is its own reviewed row that the UI row depends on. task-96957529 also carries a rail forbidding policy work outright, which is why its worker landed the offer and stopped here rather than greening its own e2e by widening a fence.

SCOPE: the narrowest widening already in the tree, mirroring 6d5db404 arm for arm. A paired HUMAN WITHOUT ADMIN must still get OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED. `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS`, `wiredMcpToolKinds()` and the MCP count pins stay byte-identical — the kind's trustworthiness on principal identity alone depends on it staying MCP-unreachable. The operator-credential path is unchanged. Nothing about the offer, the store, the payload roster or the wrapper's spawn resolution needs to move; they are landed and green.

WHEN THIS LANDS, ONE LINE UNPARKS THE PROOF: tests/e2e/control-room/agent-provider-seats.spec.ts asserts the refusal code today and says so in its comment. Flip it to the round trip — click codex, expect `cr.sessions.provider.recorded`, expect the `cr.sessions.provider.configured` line to come back saying codex on the panel's own 5s poll from /sessions/read. The durable write path itself is already proven live (HTTP 200 AGENT_PROVIDER_SET over the real command edge, mem:task-task-117a3cd9-handoff), so this row moves authorization only.

implementationPlan.description: WIDEN EXACTLY ONE KIND, AT ONE LINE. In `daemon-command-registry.ts`, extend the fence's widening disjunct (:356-360) with an arm that fires ONLY for `AGENT_PROVIDER_COMMAND_KIND`, and only when the principal is a durable HUMAN (`isDurableHumanPrincipal(store, principal.principalId)`) AND EXPLICITLY holds `project.admin` (read from `principal.capabilities`). The explicit ADMIN check is REQUIRED even though the ingress already enforces the capability: it is defence in depth, and it is the thing DoD 2's drill removes — without it the row's central security claim has nothing to test. A paired HUMAN missing either condition does not match the disjunct and falls through to the EXISTING refusal, which is why this shape yields `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED @ DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION` with NO new code and NO new layer constant. Extend the existing comment block to say which kind was added, that it requires ADMIN where the neighbouring four do not, and that it holds only while the kind stays MCP-excluded. Do NOT add a second kind, do not touch the four existing ones, and do not alter the operator-credential path.

The file's existing `refusalOf()` helper reads `outcome.refusal` and would have thrown "expected a port refusal carrying code and layer" on this arm, so arm 4 asserts the real shape directly and the comment records the divergence. Same authority, different field name; asserting the plan's spelling would have been a red on correct code.

planningNotes.risks:
DoD 1's NEGATIVE ARM IS NOT SATISFIABLE OVER HTTP, AND WRITING IT THERE WOULD BE VACUOUS — the single most important thing on this row. DoD 1 asks that a paired HUMAN WITHOUT ADMIN still refuse `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED @ DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION`. Measured: such a principal is refused `CAPABILITY_DENIED @ AUTHORIZE` by `http-command-ingress.ts:158` and never reaches the fence. An e2e arm asserting "the no-ADMIN browser was refused" would therefore go green ON THE INGRESS LAYER and STAY GREEN even if this row's ADMIN check were deleted outright — which would also make DoD 2's drill fail to redden. This is precisely the failure global rail 1 names: a second refusal layer answers first and the test no longer tests its subject.

RESOLUTION, and the plan implements it: assert the no-ADMIN case AT THE REGISTRY HANDLER SEAM (a direct handler call with a durable-HUMAN principal whose capabilities omit `project.admin`), where the fence really answers and where the drill reddens it. Then ALSO pin the HTTP layer's own answer, `CAPABILITY_DENIED @ AUTHORIZE`, in a separate arm. Both layers named, neither able to stand in for the other — which is what "which layer refused" means in global rail 1.

THE DRILL IS THE ROW'S CENTRAL EVIDENCE (DoD 2). Removing the ADMIN check must redden a NAMED arm. Run it on the handler-seam arm, not the HTTP one, for the reason above. `daemon-command-registry.ts` is TRACKED, so `git diff -- <path>` is a valid restore proof — but record `git status --porcelain` on the exact path before drilling anyway, and if any new file is mutated, prove that restore by SHA256 against an out-of-tree backup in a call SEPARATE from the restore.

SCOPE IS THE SECURITY PROPERTY HERE (task rail 1). Exactly one kind moves. Widening a second kind, relaxing the ADMIN requirement, or touching the MCP exclusion must be refused, not negotiated.
